it starts with childhood modeling of relationships. if mom and dad fight a lot, than the kids will grow up to either be abusive or to be attracted to abusive people AND both are comfortable with abuse. this is the #1 reason why people tolerate abusive relationships, because they grew up with parents who had an abusive relationship. the #2 reason is they grew up with a parent and a step-parent with an abusive relationship (this may be passing the other and be #1 soon enough do to high divorce rates).

eventually they will get old enough to have a relationship of their own. it is possible that their parents do not approve and that they hide this relationship, in which case it is possible the relationship becomes abusive and they opt to stay in it. it is also possible that their peers acceptance of them is only made possible through maintaining the relationship in which case it can also be abusive. if the child/young adult does not have abusive parental models they may learn to become comfortable in abusive relationships through one of these ways. it is much less likely than that they were raised by abusive parental models, but it is still common enough. this learned method of becoming comfortable with abuse is more likely to happen in a strict religious household that does not tolerate their children dating.

toleration of abusive relationships can be learned behavior through sibling modeling and rivalry. this is a form of "learned helplessness" and has to do with another sibling being accepted more than the one who learns to take love where they can find it. these kinds of people are at a much higher rate than normal to be diagnosed with borderline personality disorder. they have mental blocks and low self esteem because in their childhood they learned that they were unlovable and that a sibling is simply a better and more deserving person than they are. they choose to be with abusive people because inwardly they believe that they deserve to be abused. these people are the hardest to try and get them to leave an abusive relationship, they have a sort of martyr complex. even if they do leave an abusive relationship, it will only be to search for a different abusive one. they will never be comfortable in a non-abusive relationship.

they had an eating disorder. these are the ones that really piss you off. because if they had an eating disorder, likely they are perfectionists. they had a neglectful parent that they loved (they were daddies girl or mommies girl and daddy or mommy didn't love them enough, so they tried harder and harder and harder and harder to earn that love). these ones are just trying to "fix" the abusive person and giving that person the love that their chosen parent didn't give them.

they are addicted to drugs. its not something mellow like marijuana, they are a full blown alcoholic, meth addict, heroine addict or some other addictive drug. these are innate thrill seekers, and they love the highs and lows that abusive relationships provide. they are sex addicts and they get off on makeup sex. they need abusive relationships to set a background of shit in order for them to find excitement in life, otherwise sex would just be sex, it is so much more in the context of not getting the shit beat out of you. these types are crazy, don't try to save them or they will destroy you in the process of trying to have fun.

that is more or less the vast majority of them. the left overs are people who have no better alternatives and are very easy to save (just give them a better alternative). these people make up a tiny insignificant portion of people in abusive relationships, yet they are the people everyone expects "people in abusive relationships" to be like. most people in abusive relationships are not this.
